Material: UNKNOWN MATERIAL
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: DUKE ENERGY
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 38.852478, -84.223905 (Approximated from intersection)
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTING A RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN CHEMICAL ONTO THE GROUND THAT IS KILLING VEGETATION ON THE CALLER"S PROPERTY. CALLER STATED THIS OCCURRED AS A RESULT OF THE ELECTRICAL PROVIDER HIRING A THIRD PARTY CONTRACTOR TO TEND TO/CLEAR BRUSH ALONG THE ROADSIDE THAT MAY EFFECT POWER POLES. THE CONTRACTOR DID NOT APPEAR TO PHYSICALLY CLEAR BRUSH BUT INSTEAD RELEASED SOME MATERIAL THAT HAS KILLED VEGETATION (BRUSH AND TREES) FOR MILES ALONG SEVERAL ROADS IN THE COUNTY AFFECTING THE PERSONAL PROPERTY OF NUMEROUS RESIDENTS. CALLER STATED US-52, SR-743 AND SR-756 ALL HAVE SEVERAL MILES OF DEAD VEGETATION AS A RESULT OF THIS RELEASE. CALLER STATED THE THIRD PARTY CONTRACTOR CONTACTED CALLER TO INQUIRE ABOUT CALLER"S CONCERNS. THE CONTRACTOR WOULD NOT STATE THE PRODUCT USED.

properties.content:

Nearest City: Albertville, AL
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: WATER AND PULP FIBER SOLUTION
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: HUHTAMAKI, INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 2000 gallons
POWER FAILURE AT THE PLANT CAUSED BY AN ELECTRICAL STORM RESULTED IN A DISCHARGE OF APPROXIMATELY 2,000 GALLONS OF WATER MIXED WITH PULP FIBERS TO THE STREAM ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE PROPERTY. DISCHARGE WAS DUE TO PUMPS SHUTTING DOWN DUE TO LOSS OF POWER AND A SUMP PUMP COUPLING FAILURE AT THE WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT. THE SUMP PUMP WAS REPAIRED TO STOP THE OVERFLOW CONDITION. DUE TO THE HEAVY RAIN IN THE AREA, THE STREAM HAD A VERY HIGH FLOW RATE AT THE TIME SO NO RESIDUAL EFFECTS ARE PRESENT IN THE STREAM AND WE WOULD EXPECT NO ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT.

DATE: APRIL 7, 2013 LOCATION: DESTROYED TAYLOR PLATFORM - LOUISIANA'S BIRD FOOT REGION CONFIDENCE: HIGH (LOW, MEDIUM OR HIGH ANALYSIS SUMMARY: - AN AREA OF SUSPECTED OIL WAS DETECTED ORIGINATING FROM THE DESTROYED TAYLOR PLATFORM NEAR LOUISIANA'S BIRD FOOT REGION. THIS SUSPECTED OIL WAS ALSO VISIBLE IN TODAY'S MODIS TERRA IMAGE, BUT THE LANDSAT-7 IMAGE PROVIDED MORE DETAIL OF THE EXTENT OF OIL. THE OIL SLICK EXTENDED ABOUT 14.4 KILOMETERS TO THE SOUTHWEST, COHERENT WITH THE DIRECTION OF THE OCEAN'S SURFACE CURRENTS. THE SLICK EXHIBITED A SHIMMERY APPEARANCE ALONG ITS NORTHERN EDGE WHERE IT APPEARED ITS THICKEST AND THEN FEATHERED OUT TOWARDS THE SOUTH AND EAST ABOUT 1.7 KILOMETERS, WHICH CORRESPONDS WELL WITH DIRECTION OF THE SURFACE WINDS IN THE AREA.
